chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man hears testimony but was not called to witness upon it, he has the choice: if he wishes he may testify, and if he wishes he may remain silent.
And he said: When he was made to witness it, there would be for him no option except that he testify.

key_terms.أُشْهِدَ: Was made to witness, was formally appointed as a witness — passive form indicating formal invitation to witness
key_terms.الشَّهَادَة: Testimony, witness — the formal legal act of witnessing and giving evidence in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.الْخِيَار: Choice, option, discretion — the legal concept of permissible alternatives, here granting freedom whether to testify

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about someone who heard testimony without being formally asked to witness it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a key distinction in Islamic jurisprudence regarding testimony: a person who inadvertently overhears testimony has the discretionary option to testify or remain silent. However, one who was formally invited to witness an event is legally obligated to provide testimony when called upon. This ruling clarifies the binding nature of formal witnessing versus incidental hearing in Islamic law, protecting individuals from being burdened by testimony they were never invited to bear while holding accountable those who were formally entrusted as witnesses.
